title: Foundation — Bodyweight Beginner
subtitle: Full-body base building, no equipment
coaching_note: This is your entry point — the goal is consistency, not intensity. Every movement here is a building block for harder training later. If a rep count feels too easy, that's fine this week. Don't add reps on your own; we'll progress it together.

exercises.name: Marching in place
exercises.form_cue: Drive knees up to hip height, swing arms naturally. Land soft on the balls of your feet.
exercises.why: Raises heart rate and gets blood into the legs before anything else loads them.

exercises.name: Arm circles
exercises.form_cue: Small circles first, then build to big ones. Both directions, 15 seconds each way.
exercises.why: Loosens the shoulder joint before push-ups load it.

exercises.name: Bodyweight squat to stand
exercises.form_cue: Feet shoulder-width, sit back like you're reaching for a chair. Go as low as feels controlled — don't force depth yet.
exercises.why: Rehearses the squat pattern you'll load in the main block, at zero weight.

phases.name: Main Block
phases.coaching_note: Two rounds through this list. Rest as needed between exercises — quality over speed today.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Squat
exercises.form_cue: Chest up, knees track over toes, weight in your heels. Stand all the way up between reps — don't half-rep.
exercises.why: Builds the quad and glute strength every other lower-body movement will stack on top of.

exercises.name: Incline Push-up (hands on couch or table)
exercises.form_cue: Hands on a stable raised surface, body in a straight line from head to heel. Lower chest to the surface, push back up fully.
exercises.why: The incline reduces the load compared to a floor push-up so you can build real reps with clean form — that's what earns you the floor version.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.form_cue: Feet flat, knees bent. Drive through your heels and squeeze your glutes hard at the top. Don't arch through the lower back to get there.
exercises.why: Wakes up glutes that sitting all day switches off — protects your lower back in every other lower-body exercise.

exercises.name: Standing Row (towel pull)
exercises.form_cue: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or doorframe, lean back, pull chest toward your hands, squeeze shoulder blades together.
exercises.why: Balances out all the pushing you do in daily life and in push-ups — a weak upper back is where posture problems start.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.form_cue: Lying on your back, lower back pressed into the floor the whole time. Extend opposite arm and leg slowly, return, switch sides.
exercises.why: Teaches your core to resist movement instead of just crunching — the kind of strength that protects your spine under real load.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Hold your ankle behind you, knees together, gentle pull. Hold a wall if you're wobbly.
exercises.why: Quads did a lot of work in the squats — give them a stretch before they tighten up overnight.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.form_cue: Knees wide, hips back to heels, arms extended forward, forehead down. Breathe slow.
exercises.why: Decompresses the spine and brings your heart rate down before you're done.

progression_notes: Once 2x8 incline push-ups feels easy across two sessions, lower the incline (try a chair instead of a couch, then the floor). Once bodyweight squats feel light, we'll add a third set before we add load.
